title: Encoded but Unused: Bounding the Sources of VLM Errors
summary: In this paper, we investigate why vision-language models (VLMs) produce errors by decomposing them into two sources: visual-representation failures, in which the visual evidence required for the correct answer is not encoded, and visual-utilization failures, in which this evidence is encoded but not successfully used. We propose to estimate the visual-utilization failure rate using lightweight probes and derive theoretical bounds on the true rate that account for probe imperfections. We introduce VELens (Visual Evidence Lens), a rank-based probe that traces visual evidence for both a target object and its ground-truth attribute, such as color, material, or shape, across VLM layers. We evaluate VELens on over 6,000 images using LLaVA-1.6-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B. Our method achieves ROC-AUC scores of 0.95 and 0.91, respectively, and outperforms alternative probes in both low-resource and unseen-attribute settings. Using it to diagnose errors, we estimate that visual-utilization failures account for 84.4% of LLaVA errors and 70.0% of Qwen errors, with conservative lower bounds of 77.5% and 61.0%, respectively. Overall, our study identifies visual utilization as the dominant bottleneck in VLMs and suggests that a central opportunity for improvement lies in developing better mechanisms to locate, route, and use the visual information they already encode.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 VLM 错误分解为「视觉表征失败」与「视觉利用失败」，提出 rank-based 分层探针 VELens 追踪目标物体及其真实属性的视觉证据，并给出计入探针误差的理论下界；在 6000+ 图像上诊断 LLaVA-1.6 与 Qwen2.5-VL，估计利用失败占错误的大多数。

title: Beyond Correct Answers: How Compositional Cues Shape Visual Judgments
summary: Visual question answering requires models to assign attributes and relations to the correct objects, a problem known as visual binding. Structured prompts make these assignments explicit through labeled fields. Yet an improvement from the full prompt does not reveal which labels help or how they interact. First, we isolate field-label effects across ten models and six tasks by holding the image and claim fixed. These comparisons reveal differences that overall accuracy can hide. With a relation label present, adding object-role labels helps Qwen3 but hurts Qwen2 on Spatial. Second, we compare auxiliary hints that preserve or swap the question's role assignments against a no-hint baseline. Across two image sets, Qwen3's advantage with preserving hints mainly reflects errors caused by swapped hints. Preserving hints remain near baseline. Field order further affects the harm. Third, we test clearer hint wording and direct selection of the relation shown in the image. Clearer hints improve text matching but do not consistently improve visual judgments. In contrast, relation selection partly reduces errors for some hints in Qwen3 and GPT-4.1-mini.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在固定图像与陈述的前提下，跨十个模型、六个任务系统比较结构化提示中的字段标签、辅助提示（保留或交换角色分配）、字段顺序及关系选择对视觉绑定判断的影响，并发现更清晰措辞主要改善文本匹配而非视觉判断。
AI.relevance_reason: 其字段级对照揭示模型依赖文本线索而非视觉证据（即视觉旁路），与 LVR 关注的实体-关系绑定、答案是否真正使用视觉内容直接相关，可供核查该诊断范式能否用于检验 latent 状态中的视觉信息贡献。

title: LocalAgent: Collaborative Agentic Verification for Fine-Grained Instance-Level Consistency
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress in general visual understanding, yet they still struggle with fine-grained instance-level consistency verification, where the goal is to determine whether two images depict the exact same physical object under varying viewpoints, illumination, and backgrounds. This task requires both global semantic perception and precise examination of subtle local evidence, since semantically similar objects may differ only in small suspicious regions. To address this challenge, we propose LocalAgent, a collaborative agentic framework that integrates the complementary strengths of a generalist MLLM and lightweight specialist verifiers. The MLLM first reasons globally to identify suspicious local regions, which are then delegated to a Local Evidence Verifier (LEV) toolkit for fine-grained appearance and geometric matching. LEV comprises Local Appearance Consistency (LAC), which estimates appearance similarity under illumination and color changes, and Local Geometric Correspondence (LGC), which estimates spatial correspondence under viewpoint changes. LEV returns structured scalar evidence that the MLLM integrates for the final decision. We further introduce an auxiliary-capped reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) strategy, in which answer correctness dominates auxiliary tool-use and format signals, enabling the policy to learn when verification is necessary. Experiments show that LocalAgent improves mean accuracy by 4.9% over the strongest CoT-RFT baseline while invoking a verifier on only 12.13% of samples and preserving the general multimodal capabilities of the underlying MLLM. The open-source repository is available at https://github.com/Firefly-zoo/LocalAgent-main.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 LocalAgent，让通用 MLLM 先定位可疑局部区域，再调用外观一致性与几何对应验证器获取结构化标量证据，并以强化微调学习何时需要验证，用于细粒度实例级一致性判定。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按需调用验证器、整合局部视觉证据的方式，与 LVR 关注的视觉证据筛选及 LOOK/STOP 的收益—成本权衡直接相关；仅 12.13% 样本触发验证这一选择性策略可供核查感知与停止决策。

title: DisasterRoute: Evidence-Guided Dual-System Routing for Visual Disaster Question Answering
summary: Visual question answering from low-altitude UAV imagery must deliver timely and accurate judgments to support disaster response under limited edge computing resources. Routine questions may be answered through direct decisions, whereas more challenging questions may benefit from step-by-step reasoning. However, existing research primarily focuses on improving models' visual understanding and generative reasoning capabilities, with limited exploration of efficient direct decision-making and its adaptive coordination with generative reasoning. We develop Disaster-S1 based on a vision-language model adapted to the disaster domain. Trained for option discrimination, it outputs a probability distribution over answer options in a single multimodal forward pass for fast decision-making. We further propose DisasterRoute, a dual-system routing framework that combines prediction confidence with disaster evidence to decide whether to accept the initial answer or invoke the disaster reasoning model DisasterVL for review. By allocating inference computation on demand, the framework retains the efficiency of direct decision-making and improves overall question-answering accuracy through selective review. Experiments on DisasterBench show that Disaster-S1 achieves superior accuracy with low latency, while DisasterRoute further improves accuracy through selective review at substantially lower latency than full reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 面向低空 UAV 灾害视觉问答，构建单次前向输出选项分布的快速判别模型 Disaster-S1，并提出结合置信度与灾害证据的双系统路由 DisasterRoute，按需决定直接作答或调用生成式推理模型复核。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“直接决策—选择性生成推理”路由直接对应 THINK/STOP 的收益成本与停止决策问题，且以证据和置信度控制额外计算，可供核查视觉证据筛选与动态计算分配。

title: Think-Capture: Active 3D Geometry Acquisition for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at 2D recognition but often fail to maintain consistent 3D relations across sparse viewpoints, leading to spatial hallucinations under occlusion and perspective changes. Existing methods commonly fuse all frames with dense geometry, incurring substantial computation and context overhead while encouraging blind reliance on imperfect estimators. We present Think-Capture, a query-conditioned framework that first identifies task-critical objects and then acquires their geometry on demand. A 3D toolkit lifts zero-shot masks into a common coordinate frame, and a Symbolic 3D State Abstraction compresses object and camera states into structured text. Hierarchical Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) trains the VLM on cases in which geometry either helps or misleads, teaching it when to use tool evidence and when to fall back on visual cues. Think-Capture-4B reaches 54.4% on MindCube-Tiny (+21.5 points over its backbone), 39.1% on the MMSI-Bench positional subset (+7.9), and 42.8% on ViewSpatial (+5.2). It also remains robust under coordinate and mask perturbations. The full stack fits one 24 GB GPU and serves as an asynchronous high-level reasoner on an Agibot G1. Our code is available at https://github.com/819346675/Think-Capture.

AI.brief_summary: 针对 VLM 在多视角稀疏下 3D 关系不一致的问题，提出按查询定位任务关键物体、再按需采集几何的框架：将零样本掩码提升到统一坐标系，用符号化 3D 状态抽象压缩为结构化文本，并用分层 GRPO 训练模型判断何时采用工具证据、何时退回视觉线索。
AI.relevance_reason: 「按需获取几何证据」与「训练判别证据何时有用或误导」直接对应视觉证据筛选和 LOOK/USE 决策问题，其符号化状态抽象也可供核查任务必要几何信息在内部状态中的保留方式。

title: Failure Modes of Vision-Language Models for Human Activity Understanding in Thermal HRI
summary: Thermal cameras enable robots to perceive human activities in darkness while revealing less personally identifiable appearance information and fewer details of the surrounding environment than RGB cameras. As vision-language models (VLMs), originally developed for RGB imagery, are increasingly integrated into embodied systems for scene understanding and high-level planning, thermal sensing offers a promising way to extend activity perception to low-light and privacy-sensitive settings. However, the failure modes of VLMs in thermal human activity understanding for human-robot interaction (HRI) remain underexplored. We fill this gap by evaluating seven locally deployable VLMs, including models developed for physical AI and robotics, on two person-centric thermal datasets. Our diagnostic tasks examine fine-grained action recognition, activity timeline reconstruction, and the ability to withhold unsupported answers. Paired RGB recordings serve as a performance reference, while controlled variations in frame sampling, thermal input presentation, and reasoning are used to assess whether the observed errors can be mitigated. Our results show that models can recognize broad activity categories but struggle with fine-grained actions such as coughing, sneezing, and yawning. They also produce inaccurate event timelines and hallucinate actions involving objects. Simple thermal input preprocessing and additional reasoning offer only limited, model-dependent gains. Abstention behavior also varies across models even under explicit instructions, limiting their reliability for practical robotic use.

AI.brief_summary: 在两个以人为中心的热成像数据集上评估七个可本地部署的 VLM，诊断其细粒度动作识别、活动时间线重建与拒答表现，并通过帧采样、热输入呈现和附加推理等受控变化检验错误能否缓解。
AI.relevance_reason: 细粒度动作识别失败与涉及物体的动作幻觉指向视觉细节保留和证据筛选问题，而「附加推理增益有限且依赖模型」「显式指令下拒答仍不稳定」可为 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益—成本评估与停止决策提供诊断参照。

title: SpatialBrain: Spatial Intelligence Growing from Experience
summary: Spatial reasoning requires more than access to geometric tools: a reasoner must decide when direct observation is sufficient and when to reconstruct, measure, or change reference frames. We present SpatialBrain, a framework that retains experience about these decisions while keeping its vision-language backbone fixed. The key distinction is between evidence about a scene and experience about how to reason with that evidence. 3DFusionMemory fuses current-scene observations into queryable spatial relations. A Spatial Skill Library provides reusable tool procedures, and Spatial Cognition associates task conditions with experience about when and how to use memory and skills. Completed trajectories are abstracted into process records and consolidated between task blocks, allowing later decisions to draw on earlier execution without transferring scene coordinates or reference answers. Across five spatial-reasoning benchmarks, SpatialBrain improves on direct answers from the same backbone on four and ties on the fifth. Component comparisons, experience-coverage curves, and traced resource decisions characterize how the framework accumulates and uses these resources.

AI.brief_summary: SpatialBrain 在固定的 VLM 主干下积累「如何推理」的经验：3DFusionMemory 把当前观测融合为可查询的空间关系，技能库提供可复用工具流程，Spatial Cognition 将任务条件与何时使用记忆和技能的经验关联，完成轨迹被抽象为过程记录并在任务块之间整合；在五个空间推理基准上四个优于同主干直接回答，一个持平。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时直接观察已足够、何时需重构、测量或切换参考系」的决策正对应 LOOK/STOP 与视觉证据筛选，过程记录到经验整合的流程可供核查停止与工具调用的经验式监督；但方法不涉及 latent 状态的生成与更新。

title: Generalized CycleGRPO for Fine-Grained Multimodal Understanding and Grounding
summary: Fine-grained multimodal intelligence requires models to both understand a designated region and localize it from language. Existing methods learn these directions with separate objectives and task-specific annotations. We present Generalized CycleGRPO, the first unified reinforcement learning framework coupling region understanding and localization across spatial, temporal, and spatio-temporal domains. Given a region, a multimodal large language model generates candidate descriptions and then localizes each description to reconstruct the input region. Reconstruction overlap provides a verifiable reward for captioning, while individual localization rewards improve the inverse mapping. A common region-space formulation extends this cycle from image masks and boxes to video intervals and timestamped spatial evidence, without reference captions or an external language-model judge during reinforcement learning. In videos, the cycle encourages descriptions that distinguish a target event from similar recurrences. We introduce DOVE (Distinctive Occurrence-level Video-caption Evaluation), a human-verified contrastive benchmark for this temporal distinctiveness. CycleGRPO improves SAMTok's overall gIoU from 57.5% to 68.2% on GroundingSuite and average gIoU from 71.2% to 78.7% on GRES. For temporal tasks, it achieves 51.9% tIoU on Charades and 33.3% Temporal Evidence Coverage on DOVE, compared with 45.6% and 14.8% for the Qwen3-VL initialization. These results establish region-text cycle consistency as a general self-evaluation principle for multimodal understanding and localization. Models, code, and DOVE are available at https://devinxzhang.github.io/Generalized-CycleGRPO-Page/.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Generalized CycleGRPO 统一强化学习框架，把「给定区域生成描述—再由描述反定位回原区域」的循环一致性作为可验证奖励，覆盖图像掩码/框与视频事件区间、时空证据，并提出对比式基准 DOVE 评测时序描述的可区分性。
AI.relevance_reason: 与细粒度视觉证据的使用和「贡献分配/自评监督」直接相关：循环重建重叠提供无需外部判官的奖励，可供核查其能否约束模型真正依赖区域细节而非语言先验；但工作聚焦 grounding 训练与基准，未涉及推理期 latent 状态生成与停止决策。

title: Charts as Epistemic Actions for Experience-Driven Agentic Data Analysis
summary: Data agents built on ReAct-style loops now execute complex analytical workflows over structured data, yet their intermediate reasoning still runs almost entirely through text. Human analysts instead move between numbers, tables, and charts, reading visual evidence to expose trends and anomalies that text summaries drop. We ask whether charts can serve as internal epistemic actions inside a data agent's reasoning loop, and how to teach an agent to use them. We first build \probe{}, a suite of 200 controlled tasks under four matched interface conditions, and find a persistent gap between what agents can read and what they choose to use. Agents score as well from self-generated charts as from numeric output, yet plotting access alone does not translate into consistent use. Task slices show that charts lead on temporal, pattern, and anomaly reasoning, while text leads on precise reading and conditional verification. We then propose \method{}, which distils two families of experience from conditioned trajectory rollouts. One family records how to select and verify analytical operations, and the other records when to invoke text, charts, or both. A trajectory judge scores outcomes and labels intermediate steps, and a validation gate admits only experience that improves held-out performance. On three held-out benchmarks with four LLM backbones, \method{} raises analytical accuracy and visual evidence quality over matched baselines, and backbones that never drew charts begin using them, all without touching model parameters.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 200 个受控任务探针，检验图表能否作为数据 agent 推理循环中的内部认知动作，并提出从条件化轨迹采样中蒸馏两类经验（如何选择与验证分析操作、何时调用文本／图表／两者）的无参数训练方法。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及「何时 LOOK、视觉证据是否真被使用」的问题：其「能读图但不主动用图」的差距与文本／图表分工结论，以及轨迹评分加验证门控的步骤级监督，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与调用决策的训练线索。

title: ProactEgoMem: Benchmarking Proactive Memory in Streaming Egocentric Video
summary: Today's multimodal assistants are typically prompted to interpret the visual evidence presented to them. To offload the cognitive burden of remembering across long horizons, wearable assistants should instead proactively acquire and maintain useful memory as the user's surroundings evolve. Doing so on the user's behalf requires identifying what matters, understanding the scene in real time, and initiating memory maintenance in the background while the user stays focused on their activities. We introduce ProactEgoMem, a benchmark that evaluates proactive memory in streaming egocentric video. Three tasks ground the evaluation in ambient environmental needs: Information Capture (IC) preserves transient yet dense visual information, State Tracking (ST) follows changing object states, and Location Tracking (LT) records object movements. The benchmark defines its protocol at two levels of proactiveness: the Notification Level asks for a single timely notification that satisfies the user's intent, while the deeper Intervention Level asks the agent to maintain memory on the user's behalf through an active start-to-stop tool lifecycle. Parallel ProactEgoMem-Daily and ProactEgoMem-Sci tracks contain 300/100 clips covering daily and scientific use cases, paired with 1000/500 questions in ProactEgoMem-QA, which measures the quality of the proactively acquired memory. Across proprietary, open-source, video-language, and streaming baselines, even the strongest models fail to capture memory both timely and accurately. ProactEgoMem provides a rigorous evaluation foundation for proactive multimodal assistance and for video agents that co-exist with their users.

AI.brief_summary: ProactEgoMem 提出流式第一视角视频中的主动记忆基准，通过信息捕获、物体状态跟踪和位置跟踪三类任务，在通知层与工具启停干预层评估模型主动获取并维护视觉记忆的能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时捕获、跟踪何物、何时停止」的协议直接关联视觉证据筛选与 STOP 决策，可核查其任务设计和失败分析对 LOOK/STOP 成本收益及流式记忆评价的借鉴价值。

title: VoxProg: 3D Spatial Reasoning through Voxel Programming
summary: Language models' abilities to interpret tasks and generate programs offer a promising basis for 3D spatial reasoning. Yet following spatial instructions in 3D scenes requires programs to construct geometric references that language leaves implicit. In this work, we introduce VoxProg, which formulates 3D object placement through voxel programming: a language model translates task interpretations into executable programs over local voxel views of scene surfaces. Because these views index surface geometry on regular grids with explicit coordinates and neighborhood relations, an evidence program can isolate task-relevant regions and boundaries directly from scene meshes, and a downstream pose program can measure the resulting geometry to compute a target $SE(3)$ pose. Visual and numerical feedback from execution lets the model inspect intermediate selections and candidate placements to iteratively revise its code. To evaluate open-ended placement across functional use, geometric fit, and contextual arrangements, we introduce the 71-task VoxProg-Bench benchmark along with an evaluation suite pairing perceptual Intent Alignment and 3D Physical Validity. Across VoxProg-Bench and external benchmarks, VoxProg consistently outperforms relation-based, keypoint-based, and mesh-based baselines.

AI.brief_summary: VoxProg 把 3D 物体放置表述为 voxel programming：语言模型将任务解释转成在局部 voxel 视图上可执行的程序，用证据程序从场景网格中选出任务相关区域，再由位姿程序测量几何并算出目标 SE(3) 位姿，并借执行得到的视觉与数值反馈迭代改代码；同时提出 71 任务的 VoxProg-Bench 及 Intent Alignment 与 3D Physical Validity 评测。

title: Breaking Diffusion: Parallel Reasoning with Draft Refinement
summary: Drafting an answer allows a reasoning model to reconsider each decision in the context of the others. Yet repeated diffusion denoising does not ensure that individually plausible token updates form a better answer together. We introduce Draft Refinement Language Models (DRLMs), which use a single denoiser to propose parallel revisions and evaluate a candidate draft. We train the denoiser to reconstruct every token from uniformly corrupted drafts, teaching both preservation and repair. Its predictions specify revisions directly, without a diffusion reverse transition. Evaluation requires a different use of these predictions: confidence in an existing token reflects both contextual support and evidence from observing the token itself. Using the known corruption process, we correct for this self-token evidence to estimate how well each token is supported by the prompt and the remaining draft. Aggregating these estimates yields a cavity energy computed in one forward pass, without an additional scoring model. Each round proposes a revision, reads the completed candidate in its revised context, and retains it only if its energy is lower. Across Countdown, Sudoku-Extreme, and Maze-Hard, our method outperforms autoregressive and discrete diffusion baselines. With 6M parameters, DRLM reaches 44.4% on Countdown-5 and 93.9% on Sudoku-Extreme. The results establish complete-draft parallel refinement as an effective alternative to reverse diffusion for complex reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Draft Refinement 语言模型：用单一去噪器在均匀损坏的草稿上训练，同时学习保留与修补，并以校正「自身 token 证据」后的 cavity energy 在单次前向中评估候选草稿，据能量高低决定是否采纳本轮并行修订，在 Countdown、Sudoku-Extreme、Maze-Hard 上超过自回归与离散扩散基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本的并行修订与无额外验证器的草稿能量评估，可能为 LVR 中推理状态的并行更新、候选筛选及「是否采纳/停止」决策提供借鉴线索，其对视觉证据的支持尚待核查。

title: JUICE: Unified Multimodal Modeling in Pretrained Representation Spaces
comment: 69 pages, 31 figures, 37 tables. Project page: https://ced3-han.github.io/JUICE-Website/ Code: https://github.com/Ced3-han/JUICE-Code Weights: https://huggingface.co/collections/CedLJH/juice
summary: Most unified multimodal models treat images and text asymmetrically: a pretrained language model generates text, an attached diffusion head generates images, and outputs that contain both are produced in a fixed order, so the first output cannot adapt to the second. We ask whether both modalities can instead be generated by one process that is trained on them jointly from scratch. Pretrained encoder spaces hold both modalities in one continuous form and carry knowledge learned at scale, and recent work finds them effective as generative targets for vision and language. We therefore model the joint distribution directly in these spaces. We introduce JUICE (Joint Unified multimodal modeling In Continuous Encoder spaces), a single flow matching Transformer over frozen image and text representations, in which each modality has its own noise level. Which modalities are clean and which are generated then decides the task: image generation, captioning, visual question answering, or joint generation. Controlled pretraining runs test each design choice. At equal guidance, generating text as continuous states leaves image generation intact (48.41 GenEval, against 47.86 for a model trained only for text-to-image generation), while captions lose some exact wording. Training on joint and conditional denoising together beats either alone, and semantic encoder spaces beat VAE latents and raw pixels as targets. At 2.1B parameters, with no language model initialization and at 224x224, JUICE reaches up to 0.88 on GenEval and 73.1 on VQAv2. By sampling both modalities from the joint distribution (coupled sampling), it can also draw a route on a map while writing out the matching moves. On mazes with several valid solutions, joint success rises from 54.6% with independent sampling to 93.7%, and no modality has to go first. On visual spatial planning, JUICE solves 99.8% of maps at its training sizes.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 JUICE，在冻结的图像与文本预训练编码空间中，用单一 flow matching Transformer 联合建模两种模态，为各模态设置独立噪声水平，并以哪些模态干净或需生成来定义图像生成、描述、VQA 与联合生成任务。

title: A Mechanistic Study of Automated Failure Attribution in LLM-based Agentic Systems
summary: Agentic systems have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex tasks by enabling multiple interacting large language model (LLM)-based agents to collaborate and execute subtasks in parallel. However, this collaborative structure introduces new challenges for reliably evaluating and diagnosing system failures, particularly failure attribution: tracing a system's execution to identify the agent step responsible for an incorrect final outcome. Because manually performing this task is time- and labor-intensive, recent work has turned to LLMs as judges to automate the process, referred to as automated failure attribution (AFA). These approaches assume that a sufficiently capable model can infer the failing step directly from an interaction transcript. In practice, however, direct prompting often performs poorly, which motivates follow-up work that explores various ways to improve AFA performance, including alternative prompting strategies and inference-time interventions. In this paper, we examine a more fundamental question: whether this weak behavioral performance reflects a genuine capability limitation. Using linear probes applied to internal activations, we uncover a significant \emph{knows-but-won't-say gap:} models encode sufficient information to attribute a failure correctly but fail to explicitly output the responsible step. Building on this finding, we propose \emph{grafting}, a simple manual intervention that exploits knowledge already encoded in the model to improve AFA performance without requiring ground-truth labels at inference time. Extensive evaluations across multiple LLMs and benchmark settings demonstrate that grafting consistently outperforms direct-prompting approaches, underscoring the potential of leveraging latent model knowledge for more reliable failure attribution. Our code is available at https://github.com/wendyzheng22/mi4afa.

title: How Much Gradient Does Truncated Backprop Lose in Looped Transformers?
comment: 31 pages, 4 figures, 11 tables. Code, pre-registrations and results: https://github.com/Aur-Shalev-Merin/lost-gradient-looped-transformers
summary: Looped transformers reuse one block of layers many times and are often trained by backpropagating through only the last k loops. We measure how much of the weight gradient this throws away, exactly and for every k from one backward pass, on nine looped language models, and report three findings. First, on a trained model this lost gradient is set near the output: once the loop count is well above k, it barely changes with the loop count (within about 0.03 from 32 to 64 loops on the three models we tested, as a pre-registered test predicted for Parcae). Where the backward signal shrinks, $ρ^k$, with $ρ$ the signal's fitted shrink per loop, approximates it at moderate loop counts but overstates it at long ones, because the fitted $ρ$ drifts up as the fit takes in more loops. On Ouro the signal grows, and keeping two of four loops still loses 81% of the final output's gradient. Second, the lost gradient falls during fine-tuning, by 0.07-0.22 within 300 steps on three of four models, on held-out problems too. The fall is not just the read-out's share of the gradient; training only the layers outside the loop reproduced up to half of it, and it also falls under truncated training. So a trained model's value overstates what truncation removes later. Third, we could not show that it predicts the training cost of truncation better than rules that need no measurement: on two new models it tied Parcae's cost at the same k, in a test too small to separate them.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文在九个循环语言模型上精确测量了只对最后 k 次循环反传所丢弃的权重梯度，并考察它随循环长度与微调的变化，以及能否预测截断训练的实际代价。
AI.relevance_reason: 循环块复用与截断反传直接对应循环式 latent 推理的训练监督和贡献分配问题；其「丢失梯度集中于输出附近、随循环数变化不大」的观察，可供核查深层循环状态是否实际获得监督。

title: Hidden Messages Between Diffusion Language Model Agents: Causal Evidence for Latent Communication
comment: Accepted at the DiffuLM Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
summary: Diffusion language models form answers through a sequence of revisable continuous states, but multi-agent systems usually discard those states and make agents communicate only after decoding text. We ask whether one independent diffusion trajectory can pass a compact hidden message into another and, crucially, whether the receiver uses what that message means. In Hidden Messages, a sender compresses its denoising state into four signed dense vectors; the receiver consumes them while retaining its own context, canvas, and trajectory. Removing a message tests whether the channel matters; replacing it with a message from another example tests whether its content matters. Across controlled tasks, derangement removes a +63.6-point advantage on Tiny-A2D and a +100.0-point advantage on Dream-7B, while targeted substitutions steer the receiver toward the substituted fact. On QASC with the two supporting facts split across agents, matched communication reaches 80.8%, but a wrong-example message lowers accuracy to 46.8%, a content effect of +34.0 points. The surprising result is temporal: one late transfer reaches 87.8%, exceeding four recurrent exchanges by +7.0 points. These experiments provide causal evidence for continuous hidden communication between diffusion-LM agents and show that when information is transferred can matter more than how many times agents exchange it.

AI.brief_summary: 研究独立 diffusion LM 轨迹之间能否用四个带符号稠密向量传递隐藏去噪状态，并通过删除消息、替换为其他样本消息的干预，检验接收方是否真正使用消息内容。结果显示内容替换可定向改变接收方答案，且单次较晚传递优于四次循环交换。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本而非视觉工作，但其连续状态通信、删除/替换式因果检验及「传输时机重于交换次数」的发现，可能为 LVR 中 latent 内容是否被使用、THINK/STOP 与计算分配提供可核查线索。

title: DiffResearch: Accelerating Deep Research with Diffusion Language Models
summary: Deep research systems iteratively plan, gather evidence, synthesize, and revise, making end-to-end latency a key bottleneck for interactive use. Almost all production systems are built on autoregressive (AR) language models and inherit left-to-right decoding in planning and long-form writing. We present DiffResearch, an open multi-agent deep research framework that places a diffusion language model (dLLM) at the core of every stage, and measure how a diffusion backbone changes latency and report quality. Holding the agentic scaffold, retrieval code, prompts, and evaluation fixed, we swap the backbone between an open diffusion model and a comparable AR model. Across 100 Deep Research Bench tasks, the diffusion backbone is roughly 6 times faster end-to-end, driven by order-of-magnitude reductions in planning and writing. We further introduce dFast, a decomposition mode that reads intermediate denoising states and extracts subqueries before generation finishes, providing a 1.99 times median speedup for decomposition in isolation with no loss of report quality. On the benchmark's RACE rubric, dFast obtains the best overall score among the three configurations. Finally, in a public system-level leaderboard snapshot, an instance built on a stronger diffusion model ranks above several commercial systems. We release DiffResearch under an Apache-2.0 license.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DiffResearch 开源多智能体深研框架，把规划、检索、写作各阶段骨干全部换成 diffusion language model，在固定 scaffold 与评测条件下与 AR 骨干对比端到端延迟和报告质量，并提出 dFast 从中间去噪状态提前抽取子查询。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本深研任务不在视觉主线内，但其「读取中间去噪状态做提前决策」及 diffusion 骨干带来的并行生成与延迟—质量权衡，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态的部分生成、证据筛选与停止决策设计。

title: Better Policies, Worse Verifier Audits
summary: Verifier stacks increasingly sit inside post-training and test-time compute loops. We study a specific control loop: a component verifier is evaluated on fresh policy outputs against the full success label and refreshed when that aggregate score falls. For a conjunctive target $y = F \wedge M$, its on-policy AUC is $(1-q)A_{\mathrm{own}} + qA_{\mathrm{cross}}$, where $q = \Pr[F=1 \mid y=0]$. As the policy masters $F$, $q$ can rise toward one, removing weight from $F$-failures and rewarding information about $M$. We call this on-policy audit collapse. We derive a sharp identified set, a complete-erasure threshold, and the exact point at which the audit can prefer a worse component verifier; its population optimum is the full-outcome predictor, not the component oracle. An exact oracle exhibits the collapse, a natural multi-label text control shows inversion can select a head with lower canonical $F$-AUC at the observed failure mixture, and a prediction-registered ECG study shows that acting on the audit can reduce off-policy $F$-AUC, transfer the damage to an unseen generator, and increase downstream constraint violations. Preserving own-failure support prevents the damage. Matching label-complexity bounds and a controlled-mixture audit give the corresponding repair: audit the component on its own failures, and keep those failures in the refresh distribution.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究策略改进后组件验证器的在策略审计失效：针对合取目标推导 on-policy AUC 分解与「audit collapse」，给出识别集、完全擦除阈值及修复方式，即在组件自身失败样本上审计并保留失败分布。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽非视觉或多模态工作，但其关于测试时/后训练验证器审计分布偏移、失败支持保留与验证器选择的分析，可能为 LVR 中验证器训练、停止决策和贡献分配提供可核查线索。

title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
summary: Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which selectively intervenes when a potential pitfall arises and predicts the impending failure to steer the agent away from it. PAWM is trained in two stages: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on synthetic data labeled with agent pitfalls, followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM to further optimize it in the target environment. PAWM improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite, outperforming a range of baselines. These results demonstrate that PAWM provides an effective form of world model guidance for black-box LLM agents.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Pitfall Anticipation World Model（PAWM），让 world model 不逐步预测下一观测，而是在有界多步未来内预判即将发生的失败（pitfall）并仅在潜在风险出现时选择性介入，用合成数据 SFT 加与黑盒 LLM 的 GRPO 协同训练，在 ScienceWorld 与 WebArena-Lite 上提升黑盒 agent 表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预测什么」与「何时调用 foresight」的取舍，以及抽象失败信号而非逐步观测的监督方式，可供核查 LVR 中何时引入视觉证据、以及用任务相关结果而非细粒度状态做预测监督的线索；但为纯文本 agent 设定，无可迁移的视觉内部状态证据。

title: TeachBack: Learning to Teach via Bidirectional Preference Optimization for On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enables a language model to learn from a Teacher instantiated from the same model but given access to privileged information, such as a reference solution. We find that access to sufficient privileged information allows the Teacher to generate highly accurate trajectories; however, accuracy alone does not guarantee that these trajectories are suitable for Student learning. Direct access to a complete solution may encourage shortened, reference-conditioned derivations that omit the exploration, verification, and self-correction required to solve problems without privileged information. We introduce TeachBack, a bidirectional preference-learning framework for on-policy self-distillation that learns not only from the Teacher but also how the Teacher should teach. TeachBack shapes the Teacher's generation behavior by controlling the length of the reference-reasoning suffix injected into the prompt and by varying the prompt style. While maintaining comparable Teacher accuracy, it encourages the Teacher to explore and re-solve problems, thereby reducing its reliance on the reference solution. At each rollout refresh, the shared policy generates both a privileged Teacher trajectory and a problem-only Student trajectory. A pairwise preference objective uses privileged Teacher trajectories to improve Student learning, while the reversed preference uses the Student's behavior to shape future Teacher supervision under the privileged condition. Experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning tasks show that TeachBack consistently improves Student performance over existing OPSD methods and related baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 on-policy 自蒸馏中学生从带有特权信息（参考解）的 Teacher 轨迹中学习的问题，提出 TeachBack 双向偏好优化框架：通过控制注入提示的参考推理后缀长度与提示风格来塑造 Teacher 的生成行为，使其减少对参考解的依赖、重新探索与自我验证，并用正向与反向偏好目标同时改进 Student 学习和未来 Teacher 监督。数学与逻辑推理实验中 Student 性能优于现有 OPSD 与相关基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本设定，但其「特权信息导致轨迹虽准确却不适合学生、诱发走捷径的推导」这一诊断，与 VLM 中把视觉证据或参考解作为特权信息做蒸馏、担心视觉旁路与轨迹监督贡献分配的问题可能直接对应，可供核查其教师行为塑造与双向偏好监督能否迁移到 LVR 轨迹训练。

title: Cache Locally, Recompute Selectively for Streaming Video Understanding
summary: Streaming video understanding (SVU) requires video-LLMs to process incoming video continuously while answering user queries with low latency. Recent methods reduce query-time cost by prefilling frames into KV caches during idle time and reusing the cached KVs at query time. To bound per-frame computation over unbounded video streams, these methods restrict the context available during prefill. This creates a fundamental context mismatch: the restricted context may omit information needed to properly contextualize video tokens, yet, still contain information irrelevant to the eventual query, which is unknown during prefill. We propose FrameBlend, a simple yet effective plug-and-play method to address this mismatch through selective KV recomputation, without requiring any additional training. At query time, FrameBlend re-prefills selected video tokens using query-relevant context and replaces their cached KVs with recomputed ones. Crucially, this recomputation enables shorter attention windows during idle-time prefill, substantially reducing prefill cost while improving accuracy. Experiments across three SVU frameworks and five streaming and offline benchmarks demonstrate accuracy gains of up to 3.9 pp. On RVS-Ego, FrameBlend reduces per-frame prefill FLOPs by over 20% and total processing time by 14-59% for retrieval-based frameworks, including the cost of query-time recomputation. These results demonstrate that a simple change in how contextualization is distributed between idle time and query time can improve the accuracy-efficiency trade-off for SVU.

AI.brief_summary: 针对流式视频理解中预填充上下文受限导致的上下文错配，提出免训练的 FrameBlend：查询时用与问题相关的上下文选择性重算部分视频 token 的 KV，并替换缓存，从而在提高准确率的同时缩短预填充注意力窗口、降低计算量。

title: Parallelizable Probabilistic Latent Reasoning for Diverse Reasoning Trajectories
summary: Language models relying on verbalized Chain-of-Thought (CoT) are constrained to token-by-token generation in the language space, where many tokens serve textual coherence rather than core reasoning. This entangles genuine differences in logical trajectories with superficial variations in verbalization. Moving reasoning into a compact, continuous latent space offers a promising alternative for efficiently representing and exploring diverse reasoning trajectories. However, current latent models remain largely deterministic, capturing only a single reasoning trajectory rather than modeling a distribution over multiple valid alternatives. While stochastic approaches parameterize distributions over latent reasoning steps, they frequently suffer from unstable optimization and limited empirical performance. Furthermore, their reliance on autoregressive latent prediction during training precludes effective parallelization, leading to prohibitively long training times. To overcome these bottlenecks, we propose Probabilistic Latent Reasoning Models (PLRM), a parallelizable variational framework for probabilistic latent reasoning. PLRM adopts a JEPA-style objective in which the posterior infers latent distributions in parallel from observed reasoning trajectories, while the prior learns to predict the subsequent latent distribution via teacher forcing. To model heterogeneous reasoning processes, we introduce a discrete strategy variable together with a mixture-based prior, allowing the model to preserve the Gaussian-mixture structure induced by multiple distinct reasoning trajectories rather than collapsing them into a single Gaussian. Across diverse benchmarks, PLRM achieves performance competitive with deterministic latent reasoning models on single-trajectory datasets while enabling efficient training and consistently outperforming competing stochastic baselines on multi-trajectory datasets.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PLRM，一个可并行的变分概率 latent reasoning 框架：后验从多条推理轨迹并行推断潜变量分布，先验经 teacher forcing 预测下一时刻的 latent 分布，并引入离散策略变量与混合先验以保留多轨迹形成的高斯混合结构。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽属纯文本 latent reasoning，但其并行 latent 状态生成、以混合先验承载多种 latent 假设、以及后验-先验的轨迹监督方式，可供核查能否迁移到 VLM 的多样视觉推理轨迹建模；跨模态有效性与对视觉细节的保留尚未验证。

title: BlazeVGGT: 13x Faster VGGT at 2,000 Frames via Camera Token without Training
summary: Feed-forward visual geometry models, exemplified by VGGT, have demonstrated strong multi-view reconstruction capabilities through dense global attention. However, the resulting all-to-all cross-view computation scales quadratically with the number of input views, making long-sequence inference particularly expensive due to substantial frame-level redundancy among highly overlapping observations. We uncover a topology-first, geometry-later evolution in VGGT camera tokens: shallow-layer tokens reliably capture local view neighborhoods, whereas deeper-layer tokens progressively encode globally organized inter-view geometry. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BlazeVGGT, a training-free framework for structure-aware frame-level key--value sparsification. At each global-attention block, BlazeVGGT constructs a view-level similarity kernel from camera-token relations and employs greedy determinantal point process inference to select a compact set of mutually complementary views. The selected views constitute the key--value context, while all input frames are retained as queries. This asymmetric attention design preserves dense per-frame predictions while eliminating redundant cross-view computation, allowing our method to be directly integrated into pretrained VGGT as a plug-and-play module without parameter updates. Its advantages become increasingly pronounced with sequence length: at 2,000 frames, BlazeVGGT achieves approximately 13$\times$ faster inference than VGGT while reducing the Chamfer Distance from 0.41 to 0.32. Extensive experiments demonstrate a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off in point-cloud reconstruction and camera-pose estimation, compatibility with existing VGGT accelerators such as FastVGGT and LiteVGGT, and transferability to VGGT-based models including StreamVGGT and PAGE-4D. Codes are publicly available at https://github.com/MagiciannnY/BlazeVGGT.git.

AI.brief_summary: 论文发现 VGGT 的 camera token 呈「先拓扑后几何」的层级演化：浅层捕获局部视图邻域，深层逐步编码全局视图间几何；据此提出免训练的 BlazeVGGT，用 camera-token 关系构造视图级相似度核，并以贪心 DPP 选出互补视图作为 KV 上下文、保留全部帧作 query，在 2,000 帧下约 13 倍加速且 Chamfer Distance 更低。

title: Parallel Thinking for Large Language Model with Path Diversity
summary: Parallel thinking has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by exploring multiple reasoning paths simultaneously. However, we identify that parallel thinking via Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically suffers from the mode collapse of reasoning paths, where parallel thinking trajectories degenerate into similar ones. This homogeneity undermines the fundamental motivation of parallel thinking, that is, maintaining multiple hypotheses concurrently to prevent premature loss into a suboptimal solution. In this paper, we propose Diverse Parallel Thinking (DPT), a simple yet effective RL approach for parallel thinking designed to encourage path diversity. DPT rewards the model to develop distinct reasoning strategies by penalizing the prefix similarity of parallel thinking paths, thereby enhancing a more comprehensive exploration of the reasoning space. We conduct various experiments and analyses across multiple reasoning benchmarks to demonstrate the effectiveness of DPT. Results show that DPT successfully outperforms previous parallel thinking methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance over baselines. We validate path diversity as a key element to improve parallel thinking. Our code is available at https://github.com/JiaruQian/DPT.

title: Reliability-Aware Probabilistic Fusion for Multimodal Learning with Incomplete Evidence
summary: Multimodal inputs may be missing or degraded, raising distinct questions of evidence availability and trust. We introduce a reliability-aware Gaussian Product-of-Experts (PoE) in which an input-dependent reliability weight tempers each modality's latent precision, while missing experts are omitted. We characterize how reliability and availability affect posterior information and expert influence. Across two clinical multimodal tasks, the full framework remains competitive with complete inputs and achieves its clearest mean-AUROC advantage under modality absence, particularly on HAIM-MIMIC-MM. Ablations show a substantial gain from missing-aware training and an additional HAIM improvement from reliability weighting under matched PoE, missing-aware, and consistency training. Unseen test-time corruptions are used diagnostically and reveal modality-dependent reliability-weight and latent-uncertainty responses, including failure under severe degradation. Thus, reliability weighting provides an explicit evidence-control mechanism, while learning dependable quality signals remains an open challenge.

title: Real PMIDs, Wrong Papers: Harness Design for Biomedical Claim-Verification Agents
comment: Accepted to the Agentic AI for Biological Discovery (AgenticLS) Workshop at NeurIPS 2026
summary: Literature-searching language agents are becoming a standard component of scientific assistants for the life sciences, yet there is little controlled evidence on which parts of their harness matter. We run a controlled ablation on biomedical claim verification (SciFact) with the live PubMed API as the only tool. Holding the backbone and output format fixed, we compare four harnesses: closed-book answering, single-shot retrieval using the claim as the query, a ReAct-style agent that writes its own PubMed queries, and an oracle given the gold abstracts, each with two efficient frontier backbones. Naive single-shot retrieval finds the gold paper for only 6% of claims and turns overconfident errors into abstentions without improving accuracy. Letting the model formulate its own queries triples gold recall and yields the best verdicts (62% accuracy vs. 49-59% for the other realistic harnesses), although these differences are not significant at our sample size and agents use fewer than half of their search budget. With gold abstracts, the same models reach 79-86% accuracy, a significant 17-24 point gap showing that retrieval, not reasoning, is the main bottleneck. Finally, a citation audit shows that closed-book models cite PubMed IDs that almost always exist (327/335) but are almost never relevant: a cross-family LLM judge rates only 3 of 327 existing citations as relevant to the claim, versus 67% for citations produced by the search agent. Existence checks are therefore insufficient safeguards for scientific agents. We release code, prompts, and all cached tool calls at https://github.com/saqlain2204/real-pmids-wrong-papers.

AI.brief_summary: 在 SciFact 生物医学论断验证上固定 backbone 与输出格式，对闭卷作答、单次检索、ReAct 式自写 PubMed 查询和给定金标摘要四种 harness 做受控消融，并审计引用的 PMID 是否真实且相关。
